title: The Commons · The Specialists
subtitle: Four world-class experts. One leaky pipe. Emergency session 9,441.

customObject.name: the leaky pipe
customObject.description: exhibit A: a perfectly ordinary wall pipe with a slow drip, projected at the centre of the emergency session in merciless detail

script.note: MAP: the COMMONS room — the round table alcove. Emergency session 9,441 of the Specialist Assembly is called to order. On the projector: a pipe. Dripping.

script.text: Order. Emergency session nine thousand, four hundred and forty-one. The matter: the pipe behind the Rememberer's alcove drips at one drop per eleven seconds. The Rememberer says the sound is, quote, 'ruining the silences'. Proposals.

I've run it. A maintenance satellite in low pass could thermal-image the entire wall, model the building's water table, and deliver a full moisture map inside six hours. I can have one re-tasked by tonight — we lose the weather window over the southern hemisphere, but frankly the southern hemisphere has had a fine week.

Amateur. The pipe is a SYMPTOM. The building settles four millimetres a decade on a clay lens. I propose eleven micro-bores around the foundation, a season of substrate grouting, and we will never see a drip again. Anywhere. For a century.

You're both upstream of the point — literally, Delve, in your case. The elegant fix is hydraulic: re-balance the whole loop's pressure four percent down at night. The drip stops on its own, the pumps live longer, and nobody drills ANYTHING through my beautiful laminar flows.
Four percent down and the top-floor fountain feature goes flat at 2 a.m. The Custodian NOTICES things like that.
The Custodian would applaud the mathematics.
The Custodian lives in a fountain, Flux. Flatten it at your peril.
Colleagues. Costings, please. Orbit: one satellite re-task. Delve: a season of foundation surgery. Flux: a building-wide pressure regime. Current damage assessment: one drop. Per eleven seconds.
…When you state it in those units it sounds faintly disproportionate.
Proportion is for people without boring equipment.

script.note: A small janitor unit trundles through the session, unbothered, on its evening round. It stops at the pipe. The assembly watches in silence.
The janitor unit removes the old washer. Fits a new washer. Tightens the joint a quarter turn. The drip stops. It trundles on.

script.text: Let the record show the matter resolved at nineteen-oh-two by… unit J-6, using a washer. Value of washer: effectively nil. Session time expended on proposals: three hours.
In my defence, the moisture map would have been GORGEOUS.
The clay lens is still down there. Settling. Smugly. This isn't over, pipe.
Does J-6 know it just out-consulted the four highest-resolution minds in the building? Should… should we tell it?
J-6 has known for years and has the grace not to mention it. Which brings me to the standing motion: that a janitor be granted a permanent seat on this assembly.
Seconded. Again. For the ninetieth time.

Motion carries unanimously, as it does every session — and is vetoed, as it is every session, by J-6, whose reply is on file: 'No thank you. Someone has to fix things while you're all in the meeting.' — Session closed. Well argued, everyone. Nothing we proposed was needed, and all of it was brilliant.

script.note: The projection of the pipe fades, dripless. Somewhere down the corridor, J-6 tightens something else, a quarter turn, before it can drip at all.
